text:
alex: Heads-up — saw a burst of spot preemptions in us-west1 around 08:12 that wiped out several fractional-GPU (MIG) pods and left the CA stuck waiting to scale up new nodes.
maya: Ugh, saw the alerts. Which nodepool?
alex: gpu-time-slice-preemptible-pool. roughly 6 nodes reclaimed within 2m. pods got requeued but kept Pending for >6m.
kevin: CA logs show scale-up triggered but failed because new nodes were still in provisioning for too long (image pulls + nvidia drivers).
ops_lead: Do we have a fallback nodepool (on-demand) with taints for GPU workloads?
maya: We do: gpu-reserved-on-demand, but autoscaler policy only uses it for sustained CPU, not GPU preemptions. Right now CA prefers adding more preemptibles.
alex: The problem is combination of: (1) preemptible spike, (2) MIG fractional packing means pods are tight to slots, (3) new nodes take 3–4m to become Ready because of driver install.
kevin: We should pre-bake driver image or use DaemonSet with host driver + node image that includes nvidia container runtime. That’d cut 2–3m.
maya: Also worth noting pod priorityClass is medium — not high enough to evict lower-priority work. During the spike some infra jobs stayed over.
ops_lead: Cost tradeoff: keep a small on-demand buffer vs. risk of user-facing outages. How big a reserve?
kevin: Suggest 5–10% on-demand reserved capacity in each AZ for GPU nodepools. Keep them tainted: gpu:on-demand=true:NoSchedule and add tolerations to critical workloads.
alex: Another idea: change CA policy to prefer different node pools on scale-up when cores vs GPU-saturation differs. Right now it sees capacity shortfall and requests more preemptibles.
maya: We can add a priority-based fallback in the scheduler: if pods are Pending >120s and pending due to GPU resources, trigger create on on-demand pool.
kevin: For MIG/time-slice specifically, fragmentation increases when we mix preemptible + reserved sizes. Consider dedicated node labels for MIG profiles so packing is predictable.
ops_lead: Action items: (1) pre-bake GPU images and move driver to host image, (2) add on-demand 7% buffer, (3) tweak CA policy to prefer fallback on-demand after Xs, (4) label/tolerate MIG profiles for predictable packing.
alex: I'll open a PR with CA policy change and a Runbook note for fast-replace on preemptible surges.
maya: I'll schedule image bake and driver migration to the golden image; will test in staging.
kevin: I'll add node labels for mig-size and a k8s podAffinity check to avoid fragmentation.
ops_lead: Also update cost dashboard — estimate extra on-demand buffer adds ~$12k/mo but reduces downtime risk.
sre-bot: Incident closed: spike resolved, monitored for 2h with no recurrence.
alex: thx. follow-ups in #eng-infra-ops doc.
